title: New labor curves of dilation and station to improve the accuracy of predicting labor progress
summary: Gaussian-process curves using cervical dilation, fetal station and maternal/fetal covariates predicted labor progression more accurately than time-only curves in an 8,022-birth Ohio cohort, with curve-level replication in an independent Pacific Northwest cohort. This is retrospective prediction and does not demonstrate improved labor outcomes.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process models estimated multivariable labor progression curves; mixed-effects curves were a comparator. The result extends time-only labor references by quantifying the predictive contribution of clinical factors.
organization: University of Pennsylvania; University of Utah

source_review.scope: Primary full text, including Methods and Results; primary publication record or first result-bearing version checked.

evidence.tested: The study compared multifactor curves with time-only curves and externally evaluated curve predictions in an independent regional cohort.
evidence.unknown: External validation concerns retrospective curve prediction; no prospective use or clinical-outcome improvement was tested.
